parsed.summary: The Lean theorem states the two bounds of Theorem 1.1 with the paper's constants. For n ≥ 2 and a finite simple graph H with at least one edge and at most n vertices: p_c(n,H) ≤ min{1, 2048·e^50·p_E(n,H)·(1+log₂ h)} and p_c(n,H) ≤ 6144·e^50·p_E(n,H)·log₂ n. Here p_c and p_E are infima over [0,1], defined with an explicit product-measure model of G(n,p) and Mathlib's `copyCount`, which counts subgraphs isomorphic to H. The most important caveat is that faithfulness depends on `copyCount` and on `H.Subgraph` (which includes vertex-only and empty subgraphs) meaning the paper's N(G,F) and 'every subgraph F ⊆ H'; on inspection both appear to match, and no substantive discrepancy was found.

glossary.standard_concept: product Bernoulli measure of a single subset

glossary.plain: edges of K_n on vertex set Fin n
the graph on [n] with edge set W

glossary.note: V is Fintype in the theorem, so the edge set is finite and Nat.card is not junk.
Mathlib copyCount counts subgraphs G' of G with H ≃g G'; this is the paper's N(G,H).
The set contains p=1 when |V(H)| ≤ n, so sInf is not a junk value.

glossary.plain: p_E(n,H) = inf{p∈[0,1] : E N(G(n,p),F) ≥ 1/2 for every subgraph F of H}
glossary.note: H.Subgraph includes the empty subgraph and vertex-only subgraphs. Their expected counts are C(n,k) ≥ 1 because k ≤ n, so these constraints are vacuous.
Arguments are h ≥ 1 and n ≥ 2, so the logarithm is never applied to a junk input.

lean_claims.plain: For every n ≥ 2, every finite type V and every simple graph H on V with |V| ≤ n and e(H) ≥ 1: p_c(n,H) ≤ min{1, 2048 e^50 p_E(n,H)(1+log₂ e(H))} and p_c(n,H) ≤ 6144 e^50 p_E(n,H) log₂ n.

paper_claims.plain: For n ≥ 2 and a finite simple graph H with h ≥ 1 edges and at most n vertices: p_c ≤ min{1, 2048e^50 p_E (1+log₂ h)}, and in particular p_c ≤ 6144 e^50 p_E log₂ n.

coverage.why: The definitions, hypotheses and constants match the paper's statement.

flags.explanation: The constraint ranges over all Mathlib subgraphs of H, including the empty subgraph and vertex-only subgraphs. The paper says 'every subgraph F ⊆ H'. These extra constraints are trivially satisfied (count C(n,k) ≥ 1), so the threshold is unchanged.
flags.probe_idea: For F : H.Subgraph with no edges and F.verts.ncard ≤ n, prove 1 ≤ (graphOfEdges W).copyCount F.coe for every W.

lint_verdicts.why: This is real subtraction 1 − p, not ℕ subtraction.
V is Fintype in the theorem, so the edge set is finite.
The set contains p=1 (H embeds in K_n since |V| ≤ n) and is bounded below by 0, so sInf is the true infimum.
p=1 satisfies every subgraph constraint, so the set is nonempty and bounded below.
logTwo is only applied to e(H) ≥ 1 and n ≥ 2.
Fintype.card of a Fintype is its true cardinality.
